categories.main_business_segments: Iwatani Corporation operates four main business segments: Comprehensive Energy (mainly LP gas, LNG, and related equipment for residential, industrial, and commercial use), Industrial Gases & Machinery (including air separation gases, hydrogen, helium, specialty gases, and related equipment), Materials (resins, metals, mineral resources, battery materials, etc.), and Other (covering food, livestock, finance, insurance, logistics, security, and IT services).
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages advanced gas handling technologies, including the production, liquefaction, and supply of hydrogen (with proprietary expertise in liquid hydrogen and high-pressure hydrogen), air separation, and specialty gas manufacturing. It also focuses on engineering for gas supply systems, water electrolysis for hydrogen, catalyst development for green LP gas, and advanced materials processing for battery and electronic components.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include households (for LP gas and daily-use products), industrial manufacturers (for industrial gases, machinery, and materials), the energy sector, semiconductor and electronics industries, healthcare providers (medical gases), and infrastructure operators. The company also serves food and beverage, logistics, and other B2B and B2C markets.
categories.geographic_coverage: Iwatani's operations are centered in Japan, with a nationwide network of over 300 locations, but it also has significant business in East Asia (China, Taiwan, Korea), Southeast Asia (Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Vietnam), and other regions such as the United States and Australia. Overseas subsidiaries and affiliates support global supply and sales.
categories.supply_chain_position: The company operates across the supply chain, from upstream (import and production of gases and materials), through midstream (processing, storage, and logistics), to downstream (distribution, retail, and end-user services), with a strong presence in both B2B and B2C channels.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include advancing the hydrogen economy (CO2-free hydrogen supply chains, hydrogen stations, and fuel cell applications), decarbonization (green LP gas, carbon offset products), expansion of overseas business, and development of new materials (e.g., battery materials, green titanium). R&D is focused on hydrogen technologies, renewable energy integration, advanced materials, and digital transformation in logistics and services.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through the sale of products (gases, energy, materials, machinery), equipment, and related services. Additional income streams include engineering, maintenance, logistics, and, to a lesser extent, licensing, leasing, and financial/insurance services.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include other large Japanese energy and industrial gas companies such as Air Water, Taiyo Nippon Sanso, and ENEOS, as well as global players in industrial gases and materials. Iwatani is uniquely positioned as Japan's only nationwide LP gas supplier with a vertically integrated hydrogen business, and is recognized as a leader in hydrogen and CO2-free energy solutions.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, consolidated net sales were ¥883.0 billion, with operating profit of ¥46.2 billion and net profit attributable to shareholders of ¥40.4 billion. The company has shown steady revenue growth over the past five years, with a strong asset base (total assets ¥872.2 billion) and a workforce of nearly 12,000 employees. Growth is driven by energy transition, hydrogen, and overseas expansion.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Iwatani emphasizes its integrated supply chain, technological leadership in hydrogen and industrial gases, and commitment to sustainability (CO2-free energy, green products). Its unique position as a nationwide LP gas supplier, pioneering role in hydrogen infrastructure, and focus on safety, reliability, and innovation differentiate it from competitors. The company also highlights its ability to address social issues such as decarbonization and resource security.
